cases.summary: GPU 6 and 7 show high NVLink CRC errors (4196/4184) in telemetry, matching XID 74 kernel log entry. Both GPUs share a link (per NVLink degradation symptoms), with CRC counters climbing from 50+ per 10-min window to >4000. No power caps (700W limit active), thermal residuals absent (GPU 7's high temp correlates with 83% utilization, not thermal runaway), and no ECC/PCIe errors. Runbook confirms symptoms and requires node drain.
cases.rationale: NVLink degradation causes performance degradation; draining prevents further job slowdowns. Runbook remediation specifies draining before resetting.

cases.summary: GPU 3 and 5 show correlated high power (320W/321W), utilization (40%), and temperature (45.9°C/46.3°C) with no hardware errors (no XID/BMC logs, no ECC/PCIe/NVLink counter increases, power limit at default 700W). This matches a workload shift (evidence: [workload_shift] z-scores), not hardware fault. Neighboring GPUs (e.g., GPU 7 at 68.6°C/96% util) confirm temperature/power correlation with workload, not thermal runaway.
cases.rationale: Workload shift confirmed: no hardware action required. Monitor for 30 minutes if needed, but no drain or reset needed per runbook.

cases.summary: All GPUs on node a6ci-a100-node-01 showed enforced power limits reduced to 240W (below nominal 400W) during the incident window, consistent with a power fault triggering automatic power capping. GPU 6 showed abnormal low power (55W) but remained in telemetry, suggesting it may be affected by the same fault. No XID or BMC logs were found, but the telemetry symptom matches the power_fault failure type. The absence of logs does not contradict the telemetry evidence.
cases.rationale: Power capping due to PSU fault requires node-level investigation. Drain the node to safely inspect power supplies and confirm fault cause before resuming workloads.

cases.summary: GPU 4 on a6ci-h100-node-01 shows accelerating correctable ECC errors (SBE) rising to 51/30 min (ev-124) followed by an uncorrectable error (DBE) with XID 48 (ev-179) and DBE count (ev-180). Metrics confirm 332 SBE increases and 1 DBE increase for GPU 4, while neighboring GPUs (5-7) show high utilization/temperature without ECC degradation. BMC logs show inlet temp warning (ev-92) but no thermal runaway (GPU 4 temp 43.8°C < neighbors' 67-70°C). Runbook symptoms confirm XID 48 and DBE as hallmark of ecc_degradation.
cases.rationale: XID 48 (DBE) and escalating ECC errors confirm hardware degradation. Per runbook, act before job crashes: drain node to move work off failing GPU (GPU 4) immediately.

cases.summary: GPU 6 on a6ci-a100-node-02 shows rapidly increasing PCIe replay counters (331→1385 in 3 minutes) with no thermal issues (temp avg 60-65°C), no power limit changes (400W default), and no ECC/thermal degradation. BMC logs show no errors. Runbook confirms high replays without AER errors indicate PCIe link degradation requiring node drain.
cases.rationale: PCIe replay counters increased from 331 to 1385 in 3 minutes (runbook symptom: 'replays increase steadily'). No other fault signals present. Runbook remediation states: 'Replays without errors are not urgent, but they often come before a GPU falls off the bus. Schedule a drain.'

cases.summary: GPU 6 on a6ci-h100-node-04 showed accelerating correctable ECC errors (SBE) peaking at 56/30min, followed by an uncorrectable error (DBE) with XID 48 (DBE ECC error). Power limit remained at default (700W), temperatures stayed within normal range (64-69°C), and neighboring GPUs showed no similar error trends. This matches the runbook's escalation criteria for sev1 on DBE (XID 48).
cases.rationale: The runbook states sev1 escalation on DBE (XID 48) and requires hardware replacement. The accelerating SBE rate (52-56/30min) and confirmed DBE indicate failing memory, necessitating GPU replacement per diagnosis guidelines.

cases.summary: GPU 6 fell off the bus (XID 79) with BMC PCIe fatal error on slot 6. Telemetry shows GPU 6 stopped reporting (0% utilization, 55W power) while neighbors operated normally (380W, 65°C). No thermal, power, or error counter anomalies. Matches runbook symptoms for GPU off bus.
cases.rationale: GPU fell off bus (XID 79) requires node drain per runbook remediation. GPU cannot recover while OS is running; reboot needed after drain.

cases.summary: GPU 0 and 2 showed sustained thermal residuals (+12.3°C and +17.0°C) and thermal throttling (88°C/87°C) while neighboring GPUs (1,3,4) remained cool (32°C). Power limits were at default (700W), ruling out power fault. No BMC/XID logs found, but telemetry matches thermal_runaway symptoms (GPU 5°C+ hotter than power predicts, throttling). Cooling zone (0-3) affected, but GPU 1 was normal, suggesting localized airflow blockage or heatsink issue.
cases.rationale: Thermal runaway confirmed by telemetry (thermal_residual, throttling) with no evidence of facility cooling issues. Requires human inspection of cooling airflow/fans on affected GPUs. Drain node to prevent further job slowdowns.

cases.summary: BMC log shows FAN1 at 0 RPM (critical low threshold), causing thermal runaway on GPUs 0 and 1. Affected GPUs (0,1) show thermal_residual (86-88°C vs predicted 69-70°C), throttling (275/300 samples), and high temp z-scores. Neighboring GPUs (2-3) remain cool (31°C), confirming localized cooling failure. Power limits at default (700W), ruling out power fault. No ECC/PCIe errors. Runbook confirms BMC fan threshold crossing and thermal_residual as primary symptoms.
cases.rationale: Node requires hardware maintenance (fan replacement). Throttling active on production jobs (Sev2), so node must be drained for human intervention before service restoration.

cases.summary: All 8 GPUs on a6ci-a100-node-01 showed enforced power limits reduced to 240W (below nominal 400W) during the incident window. No BMC log entries were found, but telemetry matches the power capping policy for PSU redundancy loss (rb-015-power-capping-policy#when-nodes-get-capped). This indicates a node-level power fault requiring hardware investigation.
cases.rationale: Node requires manual inspection of PSUs; drain_node is required to safely investigate the power fault without risking further hardware damage.
